races.title: State House, District 16
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Carson Smith
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House since 2019, representing District 16 (all of Pender County and part of Columbus County). Served as Pender County sheriff from 2002 to 2018. Earlier worked as the county's Emergency Management Director, and returned to that post on an interim basis in 2020.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Smith was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, campaign donor pledges, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. The list of bills he sponsored did not display on the page we read, so we could not cite any. Ballotpedia found no endorsements for him in 2024 or 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. We found no controversies or foreign ties.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Pender County sheriff for 16 years (2002–2018), earlier Pender County Emergency Management Director, interim Emergency Management Director in 2020, and NC House member since January 2019, including a term as vice chair of Appropriations.
qual.why: He has about seven years of prior legislative service plus 16 years as an elected county sheriff, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee posts were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Jim Harris
cands.bio: Jim Harris is the 2026 Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 16. He is retired, with a finance degree and an MBA. He worked at IBM and then as International Marketing Manager at Intel. He lives in Hampstead and chairs the Democratic Party of Pender County. He has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he lists endorsements from Planned Parenthood, NC National Organization for Women, Mental Health Now, and Moms Demand Action. These are self-reported; Ballotpedia did not independently confirm them.
Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from the Sway voting groups Pender Progressives, Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy, and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We could not confirm his exact birthplace; he says Michigan was his first home. We found no record of elected office, so there are no legislative actions to report. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, foreign or institutional ownership of homes and land, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, gun policy, abortion, or school choice. His campaign materials list teacher pay and education as priorities but give no specific proposal. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 20: His campaign biography says he grew up in Michigan and Virginia and came to Hampstead, NC in 2017, which is under 10 years ago.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He holds a BA in Finance from Michigan State and an MBA from Wayne State. He worked at IBM with large healthcare enterprises, then as International Marketing Manager at Intel. He now chairs the Pender County Democratic Party and has led volunteer groups such as his church and HOA.
qual.why: He has a private-sector management and marketing career and a finance and MBA education, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative or elected experience, and a party chair role and volunteer leadership do not raise the score.
qual.label: He has a private-sector management and marketing career and a finance and MBA education, which fits the middle band. He has no legislative or elected experience, and a party chair role and volunteer leadership do not raise the score.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: On his campaign site he criticizes the pending state property tax ceiling legislation as a legislative power grab and favors returning local control (home rule) to counties and municipalities to handle property tax equity.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: On his campaign site he says North Carolina should return home-rule-style responsibility to counties and municipalities so communities have more control over local issues such as over-development.

clean-money.evidence: His campaign website carries the line "PACs Need Not Apply" and directs donations to ActBlue online giving.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says counties and municipalities should have greater local control to address local issues such as property tax equity and over-development, rather than being subject to state legislative power grabs.
